title: Staleness/refresh process (links, standards, sources)
context: Lesson plans can go stale: OER source URLs break (link rot), standards are revised (new CCSS or NGSS editions), and source OER content is updated. A stale plan that silently contains a dead link, a retired standard code, or outdated content undermines teacher trust and may violate attribution requirements. Link-rot and standards revision are high-probability long-term risks identified in PLAN.md. The snapshot checker (task-009) captures evidence at the time of authoring; this task creates the ongoing process to detect and flag staleness, and to spawn refresh tasks when plans need updating.
objective: Define and document the staleness detection and refresh process: how dead source links, revised standards, and updated source OER are detected, how stale plans are flagged (not silently left wrong), and how refresh tasks are spawned and owned.
acceptanceCriteria: Staleness detection process covers three categories: (1) dead source links — a periodic link-check (manual or automated) detects 404/redirect errors in plan sources and flags the plan; (2) revised standards — a process for monitoring standards-body announcements and checking affected plans; (3) updated source OER — a process for checking whether the source material has materially changed since the snapshot.
Process specifies: how often each check runs (e.g. quarterly for links, annually for standards), who owns each check, and what the output is (a flagged plan + a spawned maintenance task).
Stale plans are explicitly flagged (not silently left wrong): a flag in the plan front-matter or the repo issue tracker, with the reason and the assigned refresh owner.
The process for spawning a refresh task is defined: what information a refresh task must contain (which plan, which staleness type, what needs updating).
The snapshot checker (teacher-lesson-plans-snapshot-009) is identified as the dependency: its Wayback URLs provide the baseline for link-rot detection.
Document is committed to the repo and serves as the authoritative reference for the staleness/refresh process.
resources: teacher-lesson-plans-snapshot-009 — license snapshot + attribution checker (provides link baselines)
PLAN.md — §Risks & mitigations (Source link rot / standards revisions risk)
Wayback Machine CDX API — for checking archived vs. current URL status
output: A committed staleness/refresh process document covering link-rot detection, standards-revision monitoring, source-OER update checking, flag format, refresh-task spawning protocol, and ownership assignments.
